historical_anchor: Historically TF58 struck Truk on 29-30 Apr after Hollandia; official histories state the strike objective was maximum damage to shore installations. Branch does not copy the Hollandia route, but retains an independent Central-Pacific rationale for a smaller suppression/training raid on roughly the same late-April planning clock.

US_decision.force_band: 6-8 fast-carrier decks / approximately 370-470 ready aircraft; remaining decks stay Majuro-centered for reserve, maintenance and training.
US_decision.no_major_surface_bombardment: No need to expose a battleship bombardment body merely to reproduce the historical return-route package.
US_decision.payoff: Re-suppress Truk as a reconnaissance/submarine/local-air node, collect radar/defense information, and give newer groups controlled combat experience before FORAGER.

Truk_pre_raid_working_air_state.interpretation: Japan has rebuilt a useful local node after HAILSTONE but deliberately has not re-created a fleet-scale air concentration at a known vulnerable base.

raid_result.Japanese_major_ship_loss: NONE; high-value fleet ships are not based at Truk.
raid_result.shore_effect: Radar/plot, airfield support, stores and repaired facilities are hit again. Truk remains usable for submarine/recon/local-air work after repair but is pushed back to a reduced node rather than restored fleet base.
raid_result.Japanese_local_counterattack: A small local torpedo/bomber effort is launched after tactical contact; it is broken up or misses, with no carrier hit. This is not a long-range main-fleet strike.

strategic_result: US operational success at low strategic risk, but no opportunity to destroy the Japanese Mobile Fleet. Japan loses local aviation/facilities, not its regenerated carrier cadre.
